title: this: call, apply, bind
learningObjectives: Explain this: call, apply, bind and reason about JavaScript execution and function behaviour.

understand.concept: For ordinary functions, this is determined by how the function is called. call invokes immediately with a chosen this and separate arguments; apply invokes with an array-like argument list; bind returns a new function with this and optionally leading arguments fixed. Strict mode affects default this behaviour.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding call-site binding prevents bugs when methods are passed as callbacks or reused across objects. Arrow functions behave differently and do not have their own this binding.
understand.analogy: call and apply choose the receiver for one immediate call; bind prepares a new function with a receiver for later calls.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript scope, execution, identity, and scheduling follow language and engine semantics.

explain.narrative: call supplies this for an immediate invocation. bind creates a new function that remembers the supplied receiver.

examples.explanation: call supplies this for an immediate invocation. bind creates a new function that remembers the supplied receiver.
examples.expectedOutput: Console output demonstrates the language behaviour described.

practise.guidedTask: Use the same function with call, apply, and bind. Explain when each invokes the function and what arguments it receives.
practise.independentTask: Create a small example that demonstrates the concept, test edge cases, and explain the execution or reference behaviour in your own words.
